speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Kaposi's sarcoma and fungal esophagitis, I need to rule out opportunistic infections like Toxoplasmosis or CMV retinitis. I will now examine your fundus to look for specific signs of retinal inflammation or vascular changes. REQUEST TEST: Dilated Fundus Examination

text: The fundus examination reveals granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages, which are classic signs of Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis in an AIDS patient. I will now check your current CD4 count and CMV viral load to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: CD4 Count, CMV PCR

speaker: Doctor
text: The CD4 count of 36/mm³ indicates severe immunosuppression, which strongly supports the clinical suspicion of CMV retinitis given the classic fundus findings. I will now request the CMV PCR results to definitively confirm the presence of the virus. REQUEST TEST: CMV PCR

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite the normal PCR results, the classic fundus findings of granular yellow-white opacities and hemorrhages in a patient with a CD4 count below 50 are pathognomonic for CMV retinitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis
